purpose.text: Provide website measurement and search visibility analysis through Google Analytics 4 and Search Console, support inspection of specified URLs and requests to recrawl or remove them, and preserve analysis results for a human-readable summary.

evidences.reason: The skill description establishes the analytics, search, and indexing purposes and the questions they serve.
The workflow connects structured API results, saved data, and a written analysis.
The individual URL operations distinguish recrawl requests, removal requests, and inspection.

requirements.text: For toolkit setup, install the dependencies from the scripts directory in a Node.js environment that meets the declared minimum of 18.0.0.

evidences.reason: The setup procedure locates dependency installation in scripts.
The setup helper installs from its own directory.
The package declares the minimum Node.js version.

requirements.text: For the full toolkit, use a Google Cloud project with the Analytics Data, Search Console, and Indexing APIs enabled and a Google Cloud service account with access to the intended GA4 property and Search Console. Configure the GA4 property ID, service account email and private key, and Search Console site identifier through the documented environment settings. The documented project-root .env setup assumes the project root is the working directory when the file is loaded.

evidences.reason: The setup specifies the configuration names, project prerequisites, and service account access.
The loader uses the current working directory.
The settings identify the environment values used for the property, account, and site.

requirements.text: When initializing a GA4, Search Console, or Indexing client, reject absent GA4_PROPERTY_ID, GA4_CLIENT_EMAIL, or GA4_PRIVATE_KEY and identify the missing settings. Use the configured service account email and private key for authentication, interpreting escaped newlines in the configured key as newlines.

evidences.reason: The environment reader defines the credential values and newline conversion.
The validator defines the three presence checks and returns the corresponding errors.
GA4 client initialization uses the validator and authenticates with the service account values.
Search Console and Indexing share service account authentication.
Each of the other two client initializers applies the same validation.

requirements.text: Direct GA4 reports, realtime queries, and metadata requests to the configured GA4 property. Direct Search Console analytics and URL inspections to the configured Search Console site. For an Indexing API notification, identify the page by the supplied target URL and the requested notification type.

evidences.reason: The property helper defines the GA4 property identifier used in requests.
The standard report request uses the configured property.
The realtime request uses the configured property.
The metadata request names the configured property's metadata resource.
The search analytics request uses the configured site.
The update notification identifies the supplied URL and action.
The removal notification uses the same target form with a distinct action.
Inspection keeps the inspection URL and configured site as distinct request values.

requirements.text: For date-aware GA4 reports and bulk page lookup, accept days-to-today shorthand and startDate/endDate objects, including GA4 relative dates in the object form. Preserve supplied object endpoints. When no range is supplied, use GA4_DEFAULT_DATE_RANGE or 30d if it is unset; an unrecognized shorthand string falls back to 30 days ago through today.

evidences.reason: The date section documents shorthand, explicit and GA4 relative ranges, and the configurable default.
The settings supply the effective default.
The report parser defines how objects, shorthand, and fallback are handled.
The bulk lookup parser applies the same date behavior.

requirements.text: For date-aware Search Console queries, accept days-to-today shorthand or explicit start and end dates in YYYY-MM-DD form. Use the configured default for an omitted range and a 30-day range for an unrecognized shorthand string. Send calendar date strings to Search Console; GA4 relative endpoint strings are not a supported Search Console date representation.

evidences.reason: The settings establish the shared configurable default and its fallback.
The parser specifies Search Console's date format, preserves explicit endpoints, and converts shorthand or a fallback range to calendar dates.
The request uses the resolved start and end dates.

requirements.text: For a custom GA4 report, require the caller's lists of dimension and metric names. Query the intended property with those names and the applicable date range, apply a supplied row limit, and return structured report rows with their dimension and metric values.

evidences.reason: The custom report contract specifies the required selections, optional limit, and row contents.
The report request uses the selected names and resolved range for the configured property.

requirements.text: Apply the caller's dimension filters when supplied for a custom GA4 report.

evidences.reason: The custom report interface documents an optional mapping of dimension filters.

requirements.text: Apply the caller's requested sort order when supplied for a custom GA4 report.

evidences.reason: The custom report interface documents optional sort order separately from filters and the row limit.

requirements.text: For the page view report, return screenPageViews, activeUsers, and averageSessionDuration by pagePath and pageTitle for the applicable period.

evidences.reason: The page view report specifies its grouping, measures, and date option.

requirements.text: For the traffic source report, return sessions, activeUsers, newUsers, and bounceRate by sessionSource, sessionMedium, and sessionCampaignName for the applicable period.

evidences.reason: The traffic source report specifies the campaign grouping and the measures, including bounce rate.

requirements.text: For the demographics report, return activeUsers, sessions, and newUsers by country, deviceCategory, and browser for the applicable period.

evidences.reason: The demographics report defines the breakdowns and measures.

requirements.text: For the event report, return eventCount, eventCountPerUser, and activeUsers by eventName for the applicable period.

evidences.reason: The event report defines the event grouping and counts.

requirements.text: For the conversion report, return conversions and totalRevenue by eventName and sessionSource for the applicable period.

evidences.reason: The conversion report defines the event and source grouping and its measures.

requirements.text: For the e-commerce revenue report, return totalRevenue, ecommercePurchases, and averagePurchaseRevenue by date and transactionId for the applicable period.

evidences.reason: The revenue report specifies both date and transaction as dimensions of the result.

requirements.text: For a comprehensive site overview, combine page views, traffic sources, demographics, and event counts for the same requested or default period.

evidences.reason: The overview entry specifies the four parts of the snapshot.
The overview uses one range for all four parts and returns their combination.

requirements.text: For a traffic deep dive, provide the source report, a session breakdown by source and medium with sessions, engaged sessions, average session duration and bounce rate, and a new-versus-returning breakdown with active users, sessions and conversions. Use the same period for the three parts.

evidences.reason: The traffic analysis entry names the three parts.
The operation defines the measures of the two additional breakdowns and applies one period to all parts.

requirements.text: For content performance, provide page views, landing page sessions, active users, bounce rate and average session duration, and exit counts and screen page views by page path. Use the same period for the three parts.

evidences.reason: The content analysis entry calls for page views, landing pages, and exit pages.
The operation identifies the two page breakdowns and their measures and uses one range throughout.

requirements.text: For user behavior analysis, provide demographics, events, and a daily engagement breakdown with active users, engaged sessions, engagement rate and average session duration for the same period.

evidences.reason: The user behavior entry names demographics, events, and daily engagement.
The operation defines the daily measures and applies one range to the three parts.

requirements.text: Compare two supplied startDate/endDate ranges side by side, in the order supplied. Query both with the same dimension and metric selections, keeping each original date range paired with its own report. Use date as the dimension and activeUsers, sessions, and screenPageViews as the metrics when no custom selections are supplied.

evidences.reason: The comparison entry requires side-by-side metrics for two ranges.
The operation defines shared selections, defaults, and the ordered association of each range with its own result.

requirements.text: For a live snapshot, combine current active-user counts by screen or page name, current page views by screen or page name, and current event counts by event name without a historical date range.

evidences.reason: The live snapshot entry identifies the three realtime datasets.
The individual realtime contracts specify the groupings and measures.
The snapshot combines the three current datasets without taking a date argument.

requirements.text: For the individual realtime traffic source report, return current active-user counts by firstUserSource and firstUserMedium.

evidences.reason: The separate realtime source report names its measure and dimensions.

requirements.text: Support retrieval of all available dimensions, all available metrics, or full metadata containing both for the configured GA4 property. For dimensions and metrics, provide their API names, display names, and descriptions. The high-level available-fields operation returns the combined metadata.

evidences.reason: The high-level utility is for listing both kinds of GA4 field.
The individual contracts distinguish the two field lists from full property metadata and describe the field entries.
The high-level utility obtains and returns the full property metadata.

requirements.text: For custom Search Console analytics, use the selected dimensions, period, maximum row count, and pagination offset. Default to the query dimension, a maximum of 1,000 rows, and offset zero if those options are omitted. Return rows with dimension keys and their clicks, impressions, click-through rate, and position.

evidences.reason: The query contract specifies the selectors, defaults, and measures in each row.
The selected dimensions and pagination values apply to the same dated site query.

requirements.text: For top search queries, return up to 100 query rows ranked by clicks for the applicable period.

evidences.reason: The top query contract specifies the ranking measure and count.
The wrapper requests query rows with a limit of 100.

requirements.text: For the standalone top search pages operation, preserve the API reference's stated result of up to 100 page rows ranked by search impressions for the applicable period. The ranking disagreement with the high-level page analysis and entry point help is recorded in I05.

evidences.reason: The standalone reference specifies top pages by impressions and a count of 100.
The wrapper selects the page dimension and sets the 100-row limit.

requirements.text: Support individual Search Console breakdowns by device type, country, and search appearance for the applicable period, with up to 50 rows for the country breakdown.

evidences.reason: The individual operations distinguish three alternative breakdowns and specify the country count.

requirements.text: For the Search Console overview, combine top queries, top pages, device performance, and country performance for the same period.

evidences.reason: The overview entry defines the four parts of the SEO snapshot.
The overview uses the same period for all four parts and returns them together.

requirements.text: For keyword analysis, return top search queries and device performance for the same period. Preserve the open question in I06 about whether the device breakdown must be within each query.

evidences.reason: The keyword analysis entry associates queries with a device breakdown.
The operation returns query results and device results for one period.

requirements.text: For SEO page performance, provide the skill's stated top pages by clicks and a country performance breakdown for the same period. The disagreement over the ranking used by the shared top-pages operation is recorded in I05.

evidences.reason: The page performance entry names clicks as the ranking measure and includes a country breakdown.
The operation describes click ranking and obtains page and country results for the same period.

requirements.text: Normalize bulk lookup inputs as page paths by trimming whitespace, adding a leading slash when absent, and retaining existing trailing slashes. Use the resulting paths in a case-insensitive GA4 pagePath list filter; produce no filter expression for an empty list.

evidences.reason: The public contracts distinguish path normalization from filter construction.
The source specifies what normalization preserves and how the list filter matches, including the empty case.

requirements.text: For bulk lookup with nonempty input, return GA4 metrics for the specified page paths in the applicable date range, grouped by pagePath and pageTitle. Use caller-selected metrics when supplied; otherwise use screenPageViews, activeUsers, averageSessionDuration, bounceRate, and engagementRate.

evidences.reason: The lookup contract specifies targeted page paths, optional metric selection, and the default metrics.
The report ties the normalized target list to the selected date range, dimensions, and metrics.

requirements.text: For a bulk page lookup with an empty list, return an empty row list and a row count of zero without querying GA4 or saving a result file.

evidences.reason: The explicit empty case returns before request and result saving.

requirements.text: For a single recrawl request, publish URL_UPDATED for the supplied full URL. Return the URL associated with that notification, its update type, and its update notification time. If the response omits the URL or time, use the supplied URL or current timestamp respectively.

evidences.reason: The single recrawl contract specifies the full target URL and notification result.
The publish operation specifies the notification type, result identity, and missing-value fallbacks.

requirements.text: For an index removal request, publish URL_DELETED for the supplied URL. Return the URL associated with that notification, its removal type, and its removal notification time. If the response omits the URL or time, use the supplied URL or current timestamp respectively.

evidences.reason: The removal contract distinguishes this request and its result from a recrawl.
The operation uses the deletion type and the removal timestamp, with explicit fallbacks.

requirements.text: Process the individual API's batch recrawl requests sequentially to avoid rate limits. Return the notifications in input order on completion and save the batch result as one result when saving is enabled, without also saving each notification separately.

evidences.reason: The batch contract specifies sequential processing and a list of notification results.
Each notification is appended in processing order, per-item saves are disabled, and saving applies to the resulting list.

requirements.text: For high-level reindexing, submit a recrawl request for each supplied URL in input order. Keep each submission's notification or error with its own URL, distinguish submitted from failed, and continue processing later URLs after an individual failure. Save the combined batch without separate per-URL saves. A submitted result represents a notification request, not confirmation that the URL is indexed.

evidences.reason: The high-level reindexing entry describes a request for multiple URLs and distinguishes it from checking index status.
The per-URL loop distinguishes submissions from errors, continues after errors, and saves the batch.

requirements.text: For individual URL inspection, return the target's index status and coverage, with the last crawl time and other index details when available. Include the inspection link, mobile usability, and rich result information when supplied. When no verdict or coverage state is returned, use NEUTRAL or Unknown respectively.

evidences.reason: The inspection contract describes index, crawl, mobile, and rich result information.
The result type identifies the index details and which inspection details are optional.
The operation preserves the available inspection data and explicitly defines missing verdict and coverage defaults.

requirements.text: For high-level index status checks, return a result for each supplied URL in input order with that URL's index status. Set indexed to true only for that URL's PASS verdict. If its inspection fails, record indexed as false with that URL's error, and continue with later URLs. Save the combined status check without separate inspection saves.

evidences.reason: The high-level status operation answers whether the supplied URLs are indexed.
The operation defines the same-URL verdict rule, error handling, order, and combined save.

requirements.text: For an analysis workflow, obtain structured data from the applicable Google API operations. Save results as timestamped JSON in their operation categories by default, and honor explicit save=false wherever the individual operation exposes that choice. Save combined results for the high-level operations that produce them; for date comparison, save the combined comparison without separate period files.

evidences.reason: The workflow orders API retrieval before result saving and summarization.
The custom report contract makes saving an option with a true default.
The realtime and metadata calls also document optional saving with a true default.
Custom Search Console analytics has the same save option.
The individual notification and inspection calls document the save option.
Bulk page lookup exposes the save option.
The comparison disables the two individual report saves and saves the combined result.

requirements.text: When saving result data, write a JSON file under results/{category}/, creating the category directory if needed, and return the saved file path. Name it with a YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS timestamp followed by the sanitized operation name and, when present, sanitized extra information, separated by double underscores.

evidences.reason: The workflow defines the categorized timestamped filenames.
The save utility specifies the input roles, optional suffix, and returned path.
The results directory is based on the working directory.
The filename helpers define the timestamp and sanitization.
The save function creates the directory as needed, constructs the filename, writes the JSON, and returns the path.

requirements.text: Wrap each saved result's data with metadata for its save time, category, operation, configured GA4 property ID, and extra information when present. Preserve the result data supplied to the save utility and the original category, operation, and extra information in the wrapper.

evidences.reason: The save contract takes the data to save and specifies a metadata wrapper.
The declared saved result identifies the metadata members and keeps the data separately.
Filename sanitization is separate from the metadata and data that are written.

requirements.text: Load a requested saved JSON result from its file path and return the stored wrapper, or return null if the file is missing or cannot be read and parsed.

evidences.reason: The load utility accepts a file path and returns a saved result or null.
The utility returns the parsed saved result and defines the missing-file and read or parse failure behavior.

requirements.text: List saved JSON result paths for the selected category, newest first, and honor a supplied maximum number of paths. Return an empty list if the category directory does not exist.

evidences.reason: The listing contract specifies the category, order, optional limit, and path results.
The utility specifies the JSON file selection and missing-category behavior.

requirements.text: Retrieve the newest saved result in the selected category, restricting it to the requested operation when an operation is supplied, and return null if there is no matching result.

evidences.reason: The retrieval contract specifies the latest result, an optional operation-name filter, and a nullable result.
The utility filters the ordered candidates before attempting to load the first result.

requirements.text: After the analysis results have been saved, read the relevant saved JSON and create a Markdown summary in results/summaries/ with data tables, trends, and recommendations grounded in those results.

evidences.reason: The three-phase workflow places the summary after analysis and saving and specifies its source, destination, and contents.
The results layout identifies the summary destination as the category for human-readable Markdown.
The setup places .env in the project root.
The loader describes and uses the current working directory.

issues.reason: The documented setup and the loader agree when the toolkit runs with the project root as its working directory. There is no support for requiring discovery of the project-root file from a different working directory.

evidences.reason: The general date section describes the range forms as applying to all functions.
The Search Console parser explicitly excludes GA4 relative endpoints from the required request format.
The comparison signature takes two range objects.
The realtime snapshot has no date-range input.

issues.reason: The operation-specific contracts determine where each representation applies. The general date wording does not add historical date inputs to realtime operations, shorthand inputs to the comparison signature, or GA4 relative endpoints to Search Console.

evidences.reason: The month-versus-month example maps the wording to two rolling relative ranges.
The tips repeat the month comparison use case without stating a calendar convention.
The comparison takes two explicit ranges and does not determine them from a natural-language period label.

issues.reason: The example uses rolling periods even though the label can refer to calendar months. The two-range comparison is clear, but the supplied material does not establish a general calendar-versus-rolling rule for interpreting that label.

evidences.reason: The public custom report interface promises dimension filters and sort order.
The implementation accepts both options but includes neither when building and sending the request.

issues.reason: The reference assigns each option a specific, separate function. Preserve those documented behaviors as requirements and treat their omission from the request as an implementation gap. The package does not establish how to translate either option into the Google request.

evidences.reason: The standalone top-pages reference says to rank by impressions.
The high-level SEO page analysis specifies ranking by clicks.
The click-labeled page analysis delegates to the shared top-pages operation.
The entry point help describes the standalone top-pages operation as click ranked as well.
The shared wrapper selects a page dimension and limit without stating a ranking measure.
The overview also uses the shared operation.

issues.reason: Clicks and impressions can select different rows and order them differently. The reference and help disagree even for the standalone function, and the shared wrapper does not settle the choice. Preserve both stated rankings at their source locations without requiring both rankings in a single output.

evidences.reason: The keyword analysis description can be read as calling for device breakdowns within queries.
The high-level function obtains the top queries and device performance separately.
The first report groups by query only.
The second report groups by device only.

issues.reason: Separate sitewide device totals and device results within each query answer different questions. The documentation does not settle which relationship is required; the source establishes that both types of information are relevant to the analysis period.

evidences.reason: The workflow describes automatic saving categorically and shows a filename with an extra segment.
An explicit report option allows saving to be turned off.
The extra filename information is documented as optional.
The comparison explicitly saves the aggregate instead of its individual period reports.
An empty lookup returns before any result file is produced.

issues.reason: Automatic saving is the default behavior for applicable results. The specific save controls and empty lookup behavior qualify it. The filename suffix is conditional on extra information being supplied.

evidences.reason: The analysis workflow states that summarization follows analysis and saving.
The tips suggest asking for summaries after retrieving data.

issues.reason: The workflow gives the summary as a duty for a complete analysis. The tip describes how a user can request a summary and does not make that workflow phase optional or require every standalone API helper to generate Markdown.

evidences.reason: The latest-result lookup is documented as filtering by operation name.
The implementation checks whether a path contains a sanitized operation string, which can also match a different operation with that prefix.

issues.reason: Retain the documented selection of the named operation. The path substring test is an implementation detail that can admit a result from another operation; the source does not describe prefix matching as a user option.

evidences.reason: The displayed storage layout includes the main result categories but omits metadata.
The metadata operations explicitly offer result saving with a true default.
The metadata operations save their respective results in the metadata category.

issues.reason: The displayed layout is not a closed list of permitted categories. The explicit metadata save behavior establishes the additional metadata category.
